x: His shot of Bob Beamon soaring 29'-2½" across the long jump pit warranted a whole page and is the photograph by which posterity will remember Mexico 1968--and by which Belgravians will be reminded that winning races is not the only way of bringing fame to Belgrave.
John Martin was just under 40' in the shot-putt, while the question on everyone's lips after the long-jump was: Has Belgrave at last produced its answer to Bob Beamon?
Bob Beamon's long jump and Pat Matzdorf's high jump - world records at 29ft 2½in and 7ft 6¼in respectively - are fairly feeble feats when compared to a flea.

Ed. had a remarkable flair for catching the drama of athletics in his pictures - the Bob Beamon long jump at Mexico City - the shot of Bedford and Puttemans in the Munich 10,000 metres where one cannot help feeling one is sharing the track with the subjects.
